name: LRB (Love Runs Blind)

global_influences.evidence: Ayub Bachchu, previously a member of James's early band Feelings, drew on Western blues-rock and hard rock guitar traditions in developing LRB's sound; the band's original name derived from an inadvertent misattribution of the Australian band Little River Band before settling on Love Runs Blind.
global_influences.source: Wikipedia Love Runs Blind; Ayub Bachchu Foundation biography

local_adaptation_notes: LRB's double-album debut (LRB I & LRB II, 1992) was the first double album in Bangladeshi music, and Shukh (1993)'s 'Cholo Bodle Jai' became one of Bangladesh's most enduring rock anthems, embedding Western hard-rock guitar work within emotionally direct Bangla lyrics that resonated broadly with domestic audiences.
sound_evolution_summary: Founding period (1991–1992): formation in Chittagong and rapid rise via the landmark double-album debut. Breakthrough period (1993): Shukh cemented LRB's identity as a guitar-driven hard/blues rock act with a signature domestic anthem. Later period (through 2018): fourteen studio albums total, sustained mainstream rock relevance until Ayub Bachchu's death in October 2018, after which the band's active era ended.
concert_culture_notes: Toured internationally, including the US, and LRB is cited as the only Bangladeshi rock band to have performed at Madison Square Garden, New York — a landmark moment for Bangladeshi rock's international visibility.
listener_community_notes: Core member of the 'Big Three of Rock' (with James/Nagar Baul and Ark) that anchored 1990s Bangladeshi rock fandom; Ayub Bachchu's death in 2018 triggered a large public mourning response, reflecting the band's deep cultural embedding beyond a typical fan community.
